question: In which year did the World Health Organization publish its first model list of essential medicines?
explanation: The World Health Organization introduced the very first model list in 1977 to help countries prioritize public health needs. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T2#GNS215_U1_T2_h2)

question: Why is poor software data architecture risky for a nurse caring for a sick patient?

options.A: Important warning signs can get buried in random text boxes
options.B: It forces the hospital to buy more expensive printer paper
options.C: It turns all computer monitors completely upside down
options.D: It automatically cancels all scheduled medication doses

explanation: When software is poorly organized, critical clinical details get lost in the clutter, making emergencies much harder to handle. Good design saves lives! [learn more](GNS113_U2_T5#GNS113_U2_T5_h4)

question: You notice several patients in the surgical ward getting wound infections with similar signs. What should you do right away?

options.A: Report the cluster following hospital infection control protocols and review aseptic techniques.
options.B: Discharge all current patients immediately to close down the hospital wing.
options.C: Prescribe stronger antibiotics to all hospital staff members.
options.D: Wait until the end of the month to see if the infection rate drops naturally.

explanation: Catching an outbreak early is key! Always report the cluster to infection control and check your aseptic techniques to protect your patients. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T87#GNS214_U1_T87_h7)

question: Why is it a major mistake to order powdered vaccines without ordering reconstitution syringes?

options.A: The powder cannot be safely mixed into a liquid solution for injection.
options.B: The nursing staff will be unable to document the doses on paper.
options.C: Patients will experience immediate allergic reactions to the dry powder.
options.D: The safety boxes will instantly melt when exposed to powdered medicine.

explanation: Powdered vaccines or medications must be diluted with a liquid using special mixing syringes before they can be drawn up and administered. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T13#GNS122_U3_T13_h6)

question: Which brain structure acts as the ultimate master control center for the autonomic nervous system?

options.A: Hypothalamus
options.B: Cerebellum
options.C: Thalamus
options.D: Occipital lobe

explanation: The hypothalamus is the boss! It coordinates all visceral signals to keep your internal environment (homeostasis) stable and balanced. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T5#GNS211_U3_T5_h6)

question: What do the letters in the SBAR communication tool stand for?

options.A: Situation, Background, Assessment, Recommendation
options.B: Staff, Bedside, Admission, Review
options.C: Safety, Behavior, Analysis, Response
options.D: Symptoms, Blood pressure, Action, Result

explanation: You got it! SBAR is your best friend when calling a doctor or handing over a patient. It keeps your message clear, short, and professional. [learn more](GST321_U7_T2#GST321_U7_T2_h5)

question: During which phase of spermatogenesis is the chromosome number cut in half?

options.A: Spermiogenesis
options.B: Ejaculation
options.C: Mitosis
options.D: Meiosis

explanation: Meiosis reduces the genetic material by half, changing diploid cells into haploid cells ready for fertilization. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T7#GNS216_U2_T7_h4)

question: What type of tissue lines the part of the urethra closest to the bladder?

options.A: Ciliated simple columnar epithelium
options.B: Stratified cuboidal epithelium
options.C: Simple squamous epithelium
options.D: Transitional epithelium

explanation: You got it! Transitional epithelium is great because it can stretch easily as urine flows out of the bladder. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T4#GNS121_U2_T4_h4)

question: What is the main cause behind the development of a child's behaviour disorder?

options.A: A single genetic mutation inherited from the father
options.B: A complex mix of biological and environmental factors
options.C: Watching television programs after bedtime
options.D: Poor dietary habits during early childhood

explanation: Think of it as a puzzle: genetics, brain function, and family or social environment all combine to influence these behaviors. [learn more](GNS314_U2_T1#GNS314_U2_T1_h3)

question: Which of the following is NOT a good practice when designing a community mental health intervention?

options.A: Using respectful and accessible local language
options.B: Imposing a rigid foreign program without consulting local leaders
options.C: Involving local community members in creating program content
options.D: Designing activities that fit the cultural context

explanation: Imposing programs without local consultation ignores cultural realities and almost always leads to poor community participation and failure. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T7#GNS314_U4_T7_h5)

question: What are the classic signs of a fungal nail infection (onychomycosis)?

options.A: Soft, concave, spoon-shaped surfaces
options.B: Complete absence of the nail plate
options.C: Bright blue and swollen nail beds
options.D: Thick, yellow, and brittle nail plates

explanation: Well done! Fungal infections usually make the nail look discolored (yellow or brown), very thick, and easy to crumble. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T4#GNS112_U5_T4_h7)

question: Why should a nurse avoid crushing an enteric-coated tablet?

options.A: It turns the solid pill into an unmixable powder
options.B: It changes the color of the liquid mixture
options.C: It causes the medication to dissolve too slowly
options.D: It ruins the special coating designed to protect the stomach

explanation: Enteric coatings protect the stomach lining from irritation or protect the drug from stomach acid; crushing destroys this barrier. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T14#GNS122_U1_T14_h1)

question: What is the main reason a patient with acute viral hepatitis develops jaundice (yellow skin and eyes)?

options.A: Excessive breakdown of red blood cells in the spleen
options.B: Blockage of the main pancreatic duct by scar tissue
options.C: Impaired bilirubin processing by the inflamed liver
options.D: Accumulation of white blood cells in skin tissues

explanation: When the liver is inflamed by hepatitis, it can't process bilirubin properly. It builds up in the body, giving the skin and eyes that yellow color. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T3#GNS122_U3_T3_h4)

question: A mother insists on keeping her baby's heavy winter jacket on during weighing. What is the best nursing action?

options.A: Record the weight with the jacket and note it as the true weight
options.B: Explain gently that the jacket must be removed for an accurate weight
options.C: Weigh the baby with the jacket and subtract an estimated guess
options.D: Refuse to weigh the baby until the next clinic visit

explanation: Heavy clothing adds significant extra weight, so infants should be weighed naked or with minimal clothing like a dry diaper. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T8#GNS225_U2_T8_h4)

question: What is the main medical goal of giving a patient a sitz bath?

options.A: To lower a very high fever using freezing cold water
options.B: To increase joint flexibility in patients with severe arthritis
options.C: To reduce pain and swelling in the perineal and rectal area
options.D: To scrub off dead skin cells from the entire body surface

explanation: You've got this! A sitz bath focuses warm water right on the lower trunk to soothe discomfort from things like hemorrhoids or childbirth. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T2#GNS112_U5_T2_h2)

question: Why is unmanaged variation dangerous in clinical practice?

options.A: It stops doctors from ever speaking with nursing staff
options.B: It leads to unpredictable patient care and higher error rates
options.C: It guarantees that all nurses will finish their shifts too early
options.D: It forces the hospital to buy expensive new computer systems

explanation: When everyone does tasks differently without a standard, quality becomes unpredictable and patient safety is compromised. That's why clinical guidelines exist! [learn more](GST319_U2_T6#GST319_U2_T6_h4)

question: What is the very first step in the disease surveillance process?

options.A: Mass vaccination
options.B: Data collection
options.C: Data dissemination
options.D: Policy creation

explanation: You cannot analyze or interpret what you have not yet collected. Data collection is always the starting point. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T3#GNS313_U4_T3_h3)

question: Why is a coronary angiography performed during the workup for severe CAD?

options.A: To measure the electrical rhythm of the heart over twenty-four hours
options.B: To directly visualize the exact location and size of arterial blockages
options.C: To lower the patient's blood pressure safely before surgery
options.D: To check how much air the lungs can hold during deep breathing

explanation: Injecting contrast dye into the coronary arteries allows doctors to see precise blockages on an X-ray screen. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T4#GNS213_U1_T4_h5)

question: What do we call citizens who are forced to leave their homes because of conflicts or floods?

options.A: Orphans and Vulnerable Children
options.B: Internally Displaced Persons
options.C: Persons with Disabilities
options.D: Corporate health executives

explanation: When people are forced to flee within their own country (IDPs), they often live in temporary camps and rely heavily on special community health outreaches. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T27#GNS225_U5_T27_h2)

question: After making a solid plan for your ward, what is the very next step in the nursing management process?

options.A: Planning
options.B: Controlling
options.C: Directing
options.D: Organising

explanation: You've got this! Once planning maps out the goals, organising steps in right away to arrange your staff and resources so the work can actually happen smoothly. [learn more](GST321_U1_T9#GST321_U1_T9_h1)

question: What is the main purpose of a Clinical Decision Support System (CDSS)?

options.A: To legally sign medical documents on behalf of busy attending physicians
options.B: To order hospital kitchen meals based on patient dietary preferences
options.C: To schedule nursing shift rotations and manage monthly hospital payrolls
options.D: To provide automated prompts and guidelines that assist clinicians in making safe choices

explanation: You got it! CDSS software acts like a smart assistant, analyzing patient data to give helpful alerts and evidence-based tips. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T4#GNS113_U1_T4_h5)

question: You notice three people from the same street come to the clinic with severe watery diarrhea within 24 hours. What should you do next?

options.A: Report the cluster through disease surveillance channels
options.B: Wait until ten more patients arrive before taking action
options.C: Advise them to buy over-the-counter painkillers
options.D: Discharge them immediately with oral rehydration advice

explanation: Brilliant clinical instinct! Reporting sudden disease clusters early helps authorities step in before an epidemic spreads. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T89#GNS214_U1_T89_h5)

question: When you digest carbohydrates, what is the main sugar that enters your bloodstream?

options.A: Glucose
options.B: Glucagon
options.C: Glycerol
options.D: Glycogen

explanation: Glucose is the star player here! It is the primary, easy-to-use sugar that our bodies and brains love to burn for quick energy. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T8#GNS121_U1_T8_h3)

question: What kind of services are typically provided at the secondary health care level?

options.A: Traditional herbal medicine manufacturing
options.B: General hospital care and emergency surgeries
options.C: Routine childhood immunization in village squares
options.D: Advanced medical research and space medicine

explanation: Secondary facilities like general hospitals handle referrals from primary clinics and provide more specialized inpatient and surgical care. [learn more](GST322_U5_T2#GST322_U5_T2_h2)

question: Why is IEC such an important strategy in primary health care?

options.A: It replaces the need for administering routine childhood immunizations.
options.B: It helps bridge the gap between medical facts and everyday community understanding.
options.C: It allows nurses to diagnose complex tropical diseases without a doctor.
options.D: It guarantees immediate funding for rural health center construction.

explanation: Medical jargon can be confusing! IEC helps translate heavy health concepts into simple ideas that ordinary people can easily use in their daily lives. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T5#GNS124_U5_T5_h1)

question: What does cost-effective healthcare mean in simple terms?

options.A: Charging patients double the price for basic nursing care
options.B: Achieving the best health outcomes with the fewest resources
options.C: Employing only student nurses to avoid paying salaries
options.D: Refusing to buy any modern drugs or equipment

explanation: You got it! Cost-effectiveness is about getting the best possible health results without wasting hard-earned money or supplies. [learn more](GST322_U5_T5#GST322_U5_T5_h5)

question: What is the best way to first respond when a patient bravely tells you about abuse?

options.A: Listen without judgment and reassure the patient
options.B: Advise the patient to ignore the incident and move on
options.C: Tell the patient to confront the abuser immediately
options.D: Question whether the patient might have provoked it

explanation: Spot on! Believing them, listening without blaming, and offering a warm shoulder builds instant trust and safety. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T23#GNS225_U5_T23_h5)

question: What is a nurse's main goal in family-centered HIV care?

options.A: To empower the family with tools to sustain health
options.B: To isolate the patient from family stress entirely
options.C: To take over all daily decision-making for the household
options.D: To manage hospital financial accounts and billing

explanation: Spot on! Nurses provide education and encouragement so families can manage care confidently on their own. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T6#GNS216_U6_T6_h7)

question: Which of these does NOT cause an error when using an infrared thermometer?

options.A: Bringing the device straight from a cold room into a warm ward
options.B: Using a brand new disposable probe cover
options.C: Heavy sweat on the patient's forehead
options.D: Accumulated earwax in the ear canal

explanation: A clean probe cover is what you *want* to use! It keeps things hygienic and won't mess up your reading. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T14#GNS212_U4_T14_h6)

question: What is the main reason special diets must respect a patient's culture?

options.A: To speed up the healing of surgical wounds
options.B: To ensure the patient actually eats the food provided
options.C: To reduce the cost of buying groceries
options.D: To prevent allergic reactions in the home

explanation: You got it! If a meal plan ignores a patient's cultural tastes, they simply won't eat it, leading to poor nutrition. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T7#GNS324_U3_T7_h3)

question: Why is it important for clinical nurses to understand the basics of health financing and donor aid?

options.A: It qualifies them to replace the Minister of Health during political disputes
options.B: It helps them manage facility resources efficiently and advocate for better patient care
options.C: It allows them to collect personal taxes from patients at the hospital gate
options.D: It legally exempts them from performing bedside nursing procedures

explanation: Knowing how funding works helps nurses navigate drug shortages, use grants wisely, and speak up for sustainable patient care. [learn more](GST322_U4_T12#GST322_U4_T12_h7)

question: What is the main superpower of community herd immunity?

options.A: Reducing the cost of hospital building construction
options.B: Protecting vulnerable individuals who cannot be vaccinated
options.C: Eliminating the need for clean water and sanitation
options.D: Ensuring every adult receives an annual booster shot

explanation: When most people around are immunized, it builds a protective shield around babies or sick individuals who cannot take vaccines yet. Brilliant concept to master! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T72#GNS214_U1_T72_h1)

question: Why do persons with physical disabilities often struggle to get loans from regular commercial banks?

options.A: Government laws require all loans to be interest-free
options.B: Microfinance banks are legally banned from helping them
options.C: Banks often view disability as a high credit risk and demand strict collateral
options.D: Commercial banks automatically pay all medical bills

explanation: Traditional lenders can be rigid and prejudiced, making it difficult for disabled entrepreneurs to get startup money without strong guarantees. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T12#GNS225_U5_T12_h6)

question: What is the main physical problem for a patient with an obstructive lung disorder?

options.A: Inability of the chest wall to expand at all
options.B: Total absence of blood flow through the capillaries
options.C: Complete destruction of the pulmonary surfactant
options.D: Difficulty getting air out of the lungs quickly

explanation: Spot on! Obstructive diseases narrow or trap air inside the airways, making it really hard for patients to breathe air out fast. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T9#GNS213_U2_T9_h2)

question: What is the main reason for keeping vaccines in the cold chain?

options.A: To prevent the growth of beneficial bacteria inside vials
options.B: To preserve the chemical potency of the vaccine
options.C: To make the liquid easier to draw into a syringe
options.D: To freeze the vaccine solid before giving it to a child

explanation: Spot on! Vaccines are delicate biological products. The cold chain ensures they don't spoil and lose their disease-fighting power. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T62#GNS214_U1_T62_h7)

question: What is the main goal of a 'just culture' in a healthcare facility?

options.A: To reduce the overall budget spent on hospital incident reports
options.B: To punish staff members publicly to deter future carelessness
options.C: To balance personal accountability with the evaluation of system flaws
options.D: To ensure that nurses are never blamed for any mistakes made

explanation: A just culture recognizes that bad system designs often cause errors, while still holding individuals accountable if they act recklessly. [learn more](GST319_U6_T3#GST319_U6_T3_h3)

question: A patient calls the clinic panicking because they saw dead worms in the toilet after starting their deworming pills. What should the nurse say?

options.A: Instruct the patient to stop taking the medication immediately
options.B: Advise the patient to take a double dose to kill remaining live worms
options.C: Reassure the patient that this is a normal expected result of the treatment
options.D: Tell the patient to report to the emergency room for a blood transfusion

explanation: Fantastic! Reassure them—seeing dead worms in the stool just means the medication is doing its exact job and clearing them out! [learn more](GNS223_U3_T7#GNS223_U3_T7_h8)

question: A patient has severe burns on 40% of their body. Which skin job will be seriously affected?

options.A: Filtering blood plasma
options.B: Digesting dietary fats
options.C: Producing red blood cells
options.D: Making vitamin D

explanation: You got it! Since healthy skin is needed to make vitamin D from sunlight, extensive burns make this process very difficult. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T1#GNS211_U2_T1_h6)

question: What is the core spiritual reason behind vegetarianism in many Hindu and Buddhist traditions?

options.A: Strict government mandates enforced by ancient rulers
options.B: Ahimsa, meaning non-violence toward all living creatures
options.C: The absence of livestock farming methods in early history
options.D: The belief that all animal proteins cause immediate physical disease

explanation: Ahimsa is the beautiful principle of avoiding harm to any living thing, which strongly guides plant-based eating habits in these traditions. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T019#GNS227_U2_T019_h5)

question: What is the main goal of community-wide public declarations to stop FGM?

options.A: Forcing traditional rulers to give up their titles
options.B: Getting direct cash grants from foreign donors
options.C: Removing social pressure by having families agree together to drop the practice
options.D: Registering all villagers into the national health insurance plan

explanation: Correct! Public declarations protect individual families from being ostracized by ensuring everyone agrees to stop cutting at the same time. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T7#GNS312_U1_T7_h4)

question: Which of these is NOT a common barrier when nursing vulnerable families?

options.A: Extreme poverty pushing health down the priority list
options.B: Cultural beliefs about what causes sickness
options.C: Having too much financial wealth and multiple luxury cars
options.D: Not having money for clinic transport

explanation: Spot on! Wealth is the opposite of vulnerability. Real barriers include poverty, transport costs, and conflicting cultural views. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T19#GNS225_U5_T19_h8)

question: Why is communication evaluated right alongside clinical nursing skills?

options.A: Soft skills replace the need for formal nursing board examinations
options.B: Clinical skills are entirely separate from how a nurse talks to patients
options.C: Communication scores are the only data required by insurance companies
options.D: Nursing requires effective teamwork and clear handovers to keep patients safe

explanation: Even if you are great at procedures, nursing is a team sport. Clear handovers and warm patient communication are vital to prevent mistakes. [learn more](GST321_U1_T21#GST321_U1_T21_h2)

question: Why is constantly struggling with time management a direct path to burnout for nurses?

options.A: It forces hospital management to give nurses mandatory pay raises
options.B: It gives nurses too much free time, leading to boredom on the ward
options.C: It prevents nurses from ever interacting with patients directly
options.D: It creates constant stress, fatigue, and feelings of inadequacy from unfinished work

explanation: So true. Feeling like you're always behind drains your emotional and physical energy. Be kind to yourself—learning time management is a journey! [learn more](GST321_U4_T4#GST321_U4_T4_h7)

question: Why must health authorities provide basic food and supplies to individuals in quarantine?

options.A: To test new catering services during a health emergency
options.B: To fulfill international trade agreements during an outbreak
options.C: To comply with ethical duties and prevent people from breaking restriction
options.D: To punish individuals who fail to report contact early

explanation: Providing necessities is both an ethical obligation and a practical necessity to ensure people do not leave confinement out of hunger. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T5#GNS313_U2_T5_h3)

question: When giving the BCG vaccine to a newborn, which injection route and technique should you use?

options.A: Deep intramuscular injection at a 90-degree angle
options.B: Oral drops placed directly onto the tongue
options.C: Subcutaneous injection into the fatty thigh tissue
options.D: Intradermal injection forming a small skin bleb

explanation: You'll practice this a lot in clinic! BCG goes right into the top layer of skin (intradermal), which raises a nice little skin bleb. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T16#GNS215_U6_T16_h3)

question: How does constant stress on a very busy hospital ward affect a nurse's day-to-day interactions?

options.A: It strips away emotional resilience and shortens tempers
options.B: It forces staff to work slower and more carefully
options.C: It completely eliminates the need for formal shift handovers
options.D: It increases patience and tolerance for mistakes

explanation: High workloads and non-stop noise drain mental energy. When everyone is exhausted, even small annoyances can make tempers flare. [learn more](GST321_U5_T2#GST321_U5_T2_h4)

question: Why is keeping the 'cold chain' so important when handling polio vaccines?

options.A: To activate the chemical preservatives inside the glass vial
options.B: To keep the liquid vaccine from freezing solid in storage
options.C: To prevent the heat-sensitive vaccine from losing its potency
options.D: To ensure the vaccine changes color before administration

explanation: Spot on! Polio vaccines are fragile biological products that break down and become useless if exposed to too much heat. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T15#GNS313_U2_T15_h5)

question: Which facilities typically represent the tertiary level of health care in Nigeria?

options.A: Primary health care dispensaries in rural villages
options.B: Local government maternity and immunization posts
options.C: Private neighborhood patent medicine shops
options.D: Teaching hospitals and specialist medical centers

explanation: Teaching hospitals and specialized federal medical centers provide the highest level of complex tertiary care. [learn more](GST322_U5_T2#GST322_U5_T2_h4)

question: What is the nurse's main role when reviewing EPS results with a patient?

options.A: Rewriting the physician's surgical report for legal hospital records
options.B: Diagnosing the primary cause of the heart rhythm disorder independently
options.C: Deciding which antiarrhythmic drug brand the pharmacy should dispense
options.D: Translating technical findings into clear discharge and care instructions

explanation: Medical reports can sound like Greek to patients. As a nurse, you help break down those complex findings so they truly understand how to take care of themselves at home. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T10#GNS222_U3_T10_h6)

question: According to the Swiss Cheese Model, when does a critical incident or accident actually happen?

options.A: When holes in all defense layers align at the same time
options.B: When the hospital management changes all safety policies
options.C: When a single nurse makes a minor math calculation error
options.D: When a patient refuses to take prescribed medications

explanation: Brilliant! Accidents happen only when multiple safety barriers fail simultaneously, letting the error reach the patient. Keep pushing forward! [learn more](GST319_U5_T6#GST319_U5_T6_h2)

question: Why might an autistic patient who is hyposensitive seek out heavy pressure or spin in circles?

options.A: To lower their body temperature during a fever
options.B: To intentionally annoy the healthcare staff on duty
options.C: To practice for athletic events
options.D: To provide their nervous system with the sensory input it craves

explanation: Exactly! When someone is hyposensitive, their nervous system needs extra stimulation—like spinning or deep pressure—just to register the feeling. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T5#GNS324_U4_T5_h3)

question: What is the medical term for having an abnormally low platelet count, which increases a patient's risk of bleeding?

options.A: Anemia
options.B: Polycythemia
options.C: Thrombocytopenia
options.D: Leukemia

explanation: Well done! 'Thrombo' relates to clotting, 'cyto' to cells, and 'penia' means deficiency. Put it together, and thrombocytopenia means low platelets and bleeding risk. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T1#GNS111_U2_T1_h7)

question: What do the letters in the FAST stroke mnemonic stand for to help recognize warning signs?

options.A: Fluid intake, Activity level, Skin turgor, Eyes check
options.B: Fast breathing, Airway blockage, Sound tone, Temperature
options.C: Face drooping, Arm weakness, Speech difficulty, Time to call
options.D: Fever, Aches, Stiffness, Tiredness

explanation: FAST is a simple public health tool used to spot the most common stroke symptoms quickly. [learn more](GNS315_U2_T2#GNS315_U2_T2_h6)

question: A caregiver helps a frail elderly client move safely from a wheelchair onto the living room sofa. Which specific ADL is this caregiver assisting with?

options.A: Feeding
options.B: Dressing
options.C: Bathing
options.D: Transferring

explanation: Moving a patient between surfaces, such as from a bed to a chair or wheelchair to a sofa, falls under the category of transferring. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T4#GNS324_U5_T4_h2)

question: What is the main job of sensory receptors in the peripheral nervous system?

options.A: To turn things like touch, heat, and pressure into electrical signals
options.B: To protect delicate nerve bundles from getting crushed
options.C: To release hormones that control your blood pressure
options.D: To tell your skeletal muscles to squeeze tightly

explanation: You nailed it! Sensory receptors act like translators, converting physical feelings from the environment into the electrical language your nerves understand. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T4#GNS211_U3_T4_h5)

question: What should a nurse avoid writing inside the patient's official clinical chart?

options.A: The objective facts of what occurred during the event
options.B: A note stating that an incident report was completed
options.C: The name of the doctor notified about the patient's status
options.D: The exact vital signs measured after a medication error

explanation: Correct! Mentioning the incident report in the clinical chart mixes administrative logs with patient care records, which causes legal complications. [learn more](GST319_U4_T9#GST319_U4_T9_h7)

question: Which of these is checked as part of a psychosocial health history?

options.A: Precise surgical incision healing progress
options.B: Coping mechanisms and daily stress management
options.C: Laboratory results from routine blood tests
options.D: Blood pressure readings taken over 24 hours

explanation: Correct! A psychosocial check looks at mental wellness, stress levels, and emotional support systems. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T3#GNS222_U3_T3_h7)

question: What is the main way ordinary Nigerians pay for their healthcare needs?

options.A: Community health funds
options.B: Federal health insurance
options.C: Out-of-pocket payments
options.D: Employer-paid retainerships

explanation: You got it! Most Nigerians pay cash straight from their pockets for every consultation, lab test, and prescription whenever they visit a clinic. [learn more](GST322_U3_T4#GST322_U3_T4_h3)

question: What is the recommended compression rate per minute for adult CPR?

options.A: 60 to 80 compressions per minute
options.B: 140 to 160 compressions per minute
options.C: 100 to 120 compressions per minute
options.D: 40 to 50 compressions per minute

explanation: Aim for a steady, brisk rhythm of 100 to 120 compressions per minute. Fun fact: pumping to the beat of the song 'Stayin' Alive' helps hit this exact speed! [learn more](GNS321_U2_T6#GNS321_U2_T6_h3)

question: A nurse notices male partners sitting in the antenatal waiting room look ignored and uncomfortable. What should she do?

options.A: Tell the pregnant women to handle their husbands at home.
options.B: Ask security guards to escort them outside.
options.C: Greet them warmly and include them in the health talk.
options.D: Ignore them since antenatal care is only for women.

explanation: Welcoming men and including them in discussions builds trust and makes them want to return. Great nursing care! [learn more](GNS312_U4_T7#GNS312_U4_T7_h7)

question: What is an important nursing duty before an endoscopy procedure begins?

options.A: Ensuring the informed consent form is signed and placed in the chart
options.B: Prescribing the specific dose of sedative drugs for the doctor

question: What do we call a disease that is always present at a steady, expected level in a specific area?

question: Why is it so important for a nurse to ask a patient to demonstrate how they use their inhaler?

question: What is the most effective approach a nurse should take when providing nutritional counseling to a nursing mother?

question: Why must nurses learn about different cultural and spiritual beliefs surrounding death?

question: What is the big advantage of running a small pilot study first?

question: What causes an obstetric fistula when a young mother has a very long, difficult labor?

question: Why must you check the expiration date on the test strip bottle before testing a patient?

question: Because a pregnant teenager's pelvis is still growing, she is at higher risk for which complication?

question: A nursing lecturer uses a physical heart model to explain blood flow to students with different learning styles. Which group benefits most from handling and examining this model directly?

question: Why does patient awareness nowadays push nursing practice to improve?

question: A patient with a spinal cord injury feels worthless and asks why this happened to them. What should the nurse suspect?

question: What happens to the white blood cell count during active labour and delivery?

question: A nurse in a rural Nigerian clinic notices more waterborne diseases during the rainy season. What action best reflects PHC philosophy?

question: During a home visit, a patient with severe anxiety mentions thoughts of ending their life. What is the nurse's priority action?

question: Why do nurses care about finding the 'central tendency' in research data?

question: Why is good room ventilation a must in spaces where chemical disinfectants like glutaraldehyde are used?

options.A: To prevent toxic vapors from accumulating and harming respiratory tracts
options.B: To cool down high-speed mechanical washer-disinfector units
options.C: To speed up the drying time of washed stainless steel basins
options.D: To reduce ambient room humidity so metal instruments do not rust

question: What is the main reason potassium chloride is included in standard ORS?

options.C: To prevent dangerous heart rhythm changes from mineral loss
options.D: To thicken the solution so it stays in the gut longer

question: What is the main goal of quality improvement in nursing?

options.A: Making patient care safer and more reliable

question: How do smart beds help keep vulnerable hospital patients safe?

options.A: They automatically administer pain medication when turning

options.C: Built-in scales eliminate the need to chart daily fluid intake
options.D: Sensors alert staff when an unassisted patient tries to stand up

question: Why do nurses need to check complete blood counts (CBC) regularly for patients on carbamazepine?

options.A: To check how well the kidneys are filtering excess water
options.B: To confirm that the patient is eating enough iron-rich foods
options.C: To monitor for bone marrow suppression and low blood cell counts
options.D: To measure the exact amount of calcium stored in the bones

explanation: Carbamazepine can sometimes slow down the bone marrow's ability to make blood cells. Regular blood tests help us catch any dangerous drops in red or white blood cells early. [learn more](GNS223_U6_T3#GNS223_U6_T3_h5)

question: A patient with type 2 diabetes needs help managing their meals. What is a great, simple tip to share first?

options.C: Stop eating all forms of food for two days of the week
options.D: Fill half of your meal plate with non-starchy, colorful vegetables

explanation: You nailed it! The plate method is a fantastic, visual way to help patients control portions and get enough fiber without stressful calorie counting. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T009#GNS227_U4_T009_h7)

question: Where does Community-Based Rehabilitation mainly take place?

options.A: A secure psychiatric asylum
options.B: A large federal teaching hospital
options.C: The local community and family home
options.D: A private overseas medical facility

question: Which fluid is normally used for a washout to keep body salts balanced?

options.B: Plain tap water

question: What is the main reason nurses connect family caregivers with respite care services?

options.A: To prevent caregiver burnout and exhaustion
options.B: To reduce the financial cost of home medical equipment
options.C: To permanently transfer legal responsibility for the patient
options.D: To train family members to become licensed nurses

explanation: Looking after a stroke survivor is tough work. Respite care gives families a well-deserved break to rest and recharge! [learn more](GNS324_U4_T9#GNS324_U4_T9_h7)

question: Why is BCC so important in programs like malaria control?

options.A: People must be persuaded to consistently sleep under insecticide-treated nets
options.B: BCC automatically kills adult mosquitoes living near stagnant water pools
options.C: Insects understand health messages broadcasted over local radio stations
options.D: Communication programs replace the need for antimalarial drug treatments

explanation: You got it! Having mosquito nets in a box doesn't help if people refuse to hang and sleep under them every night. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T3#GNS124_U5_T3_h5)

question: How is the pathway of our sense of smell (olfaction) different from all other senses?

options.A: It completely bypasses the cerebral cortex entirely
options.B: It does not pass through the thalamus before reaching the cortex
options.C: It crosses over to the opposite side of the brain twice
options.D: It is processed entirely within the occipital lobe

explanation: Unlike sight or sound, smell signals go straight to the olfactory cortex without stopping at the thalamus relay station first. That's a classic exam favorite! [learn more](GNS211_U3_T11#GNS211_U3_T11_h5)

question: Why can a normal blood pressure reading sometimes be misleading in early cardiovascular shock?

options.A: Only the pulse rate matters during a cardiac crisis
options.B: Heart conditions never affect blood pressure numbers
options.C: The body's compensation keeps pressure normal before it crashes
options.D: Blood pressure cuffs are notoriously inaccurate in emergency rooms

question: What exactly is a sampling frame?

options.A: The statistical formula used to calculate sample size

options.C: The timeline created for data collection in the ward
options.D: The equipment used to measure vital signs in a study

question: What makes a 'prodrug' unique compared to regular medicines?

options.A: It is always given as a liquid injection rather than a pill
options.B: It bypasses the liver completely without ever changing form
options.C: It is given in an inactive form and needs metabolism to become active
options.D: It leaves the body immediately through sweat instead of urine

explanation: A prodrug is like an undercover agent—it starts off inactive when you swallow it, and only wakes up (becomes active) after the body's metabolism works on it. Pretty cool, right? [learn more](GNS125_U5_T3#GNS125_U5_T3_h1)

question: What is a 'confounding factor' in healthcare research?

options.A: A hospital policy that requires nurses to wear protective uniforms
options.B: A type of patient interview question that cannot be transcribed
options.C: A hidden variable that can distort the true relationship between cause and effect
options.D: A mathematical mistake made when calculating the standard deviation

explanation: A confounder is a sneaky hidden factor that makes it look like a treatment caused a result when something else actually played a major role. [learn more](GNS224_U2_T3#GNS224_U2_T3_h7)

question: Why is including a wide variety of foods in family meal planning so important?

options.A: It guarantees that every family member eats the exact same calorie count
options.B: It prevents nutrient gaps and avoids excessive intake of any single substance
options.C: It ensures the household spends the maximum possible food budget
options.D: It eliminates the need to provide clean drinking water at meals

explanation: Eating a diverse mix of foods makes it far more likely the body gets all necessary vitamins without relying too heavily on one food type. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T015#GNS227_U4_T015_h1)

question: As a community health nurse on a home visit, what is one of your key duties?

options.A: Prescribing high-risk surgical medications
options.B: Assessing living conditions and providing counseling
options.C: Replacing routine laboratory equipment
options.D: Performing major surgical procedures at home

question: What is the main goal of a descriptive research design?

options.A: To accurately document characteristics of a population or situation
options.B: To test the effectiveness of a new surgical procedure
options.C: To prove that variable A causes a change in variable B
options.D: To compare two different patient groups after an intervention

explanation: Great job! Descriptive studies are all about painting a clear picture of what is going on right now, without needing to dig into the 'why' or 'how'. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T8#GNS224_U1_T8_h2)

question: A patient with severe second-degree burns across their back requires which dietary adjustment?

options.C: Zero protein to keep the kidneys from working too hard.

question: Which lab result tells us an HIV-positive patient has progressed to AIDS?

question: Why is the normal acidic environment of the vagina important?

options.B: It prevents harmful bacteria from growing
options.C: It speeds up the movement of sperm cells
options.D: It helps the cervix open during labor

question: Why is knowing a drug's volume of distribution useful in clinical practice?

options.A: It helps determine the right loading dose for the patient

options.C: It measures the exact weight of body fat

question: What is the golden rule when writing the results section of your research?

options.A: Include your personal opinions on why the treatment failed
options.B: Focus heavily on reviewing what other authors previously wrote

options.D: Hide any unexpected data that does not match your original guess

question: What is the main goal of screening tests in vulnerable populations?

options.A: To cure advanced surgical conditions without using medications
options.B: To replace all laboratory blood tests with physical inspections
options.C: To collect registration fees from wealthy community members
options.D: To identify disease risk or early illness before symptoms appear

question: When you are checking in on a grieving family member, what should be your main focus?

options.B: Diagnosing them with a mental health disorder
options.C: Forcing them to talk about the person who passed away

question: A nurse compares the number of malaria cases between two villages with different population sizes. Why is calculating a rate better than just looking at raw counts?

options.B: Raw counts are always illegal to use in public health
options.C: Rates account for differences in total population size

question: A patient recovering from a radical hysterectomy notices a clear fluid leaking from her vagina along with tummy discomfort. What should you suspect?

question: Why does the scope of standing orders differ between a small health post and a large health center?

options.C: Government regulations forbid rural clinics from using any form of written guidelines

question: Which health check is most crucial before giving oral medications to a patient with advanced neurological degeneration?

question: Which part of the glucometer setup has the chemical reagents that react with blood?

question: What kind of air pressure do they use inside an operating room to keep outside hallway air from rushing in?

question: What is the primary goal of discipline in nursing management?

question: How do abdominal thrusts (the Heimlich maneuver) help a choking person?

question: What is the main goal of getting widespread COVID-19 vaccinations?

question: Why must nurses and doctors strictly avoid inserting fingers into the vagina (digital exam) when placenta praevia is suspected?

options.B: It introduces severe bacterial infection into the amniotic sac

question: Why are nurses considered the frontline defense in pharmacovigilance?

question: Why do many Nigerian communities rely on NGOs for healthcare support?

options.C: Communities prefer foreign medical staff over local Nigerian nurses

question: What is the main difference between direct medical costs and direct non-medical costs?

options.C: Medical costs occur in the hospital, while non-medical costs occur at home
options.D: Medical costs are paid by the government, while non-medical costs are paid in cash

question: What is the heaviest penalty a nursing council can give for severe malpractice?

question: What is the normal age range for the closure of the larger anterior fontanelle?

question: Which setting is best for an older adult who needs round-the-clock nursing checks and complex wound care?

question: How is working as a home health nurse different from working in a hospital?

question: Why does a person trapped in a smoke-filled room suffer from asphyxia?

options.D: Sudden paralysis of the heart muscle

question: What key engineering feature protects underground water sources underneath a proper sanitary landfill?

options.C: Direct connection to municipal storm water pipes
options.D: Impermeable bottom liners and leachate collection systems

question: Older adults often experience stiffer chest walls and weaker breathing muscles. What is the direct result of this?

question: What is the primary clinical definition of faecal incontinence?

question: How many escape routes should a good fire safety plan provide for each room?

question: Which hormone acts like a chill pill for the uterus, keeping its muscles calm and preventing early contractions?

question: Which question represents the core mindset shift of trauma-informed care?

options.C: When will you get over this?
options.D: Who is to blame for this?

question: A nurse is planning care for a newly admitted client with major depressive disorder. What is the best immediate action?

question: Which scenario is a classic example of indirect contact transmission?

question: In palliative care, who is considered the 'unit of care' alongside the patient?

question: A 38-week pregnant woman comes in complaining of tummy tightening that stops when she walks around. What is this likely to be?

question: Why are babies born to unvaccinated mothers at such high risk for tetanus?

question: A patient can bear some weight on one leg and needs to move from the bed to a chair. Which transfer method is best?

question: What event usually triggers an immediate public health outbreak investigation?

question: When using Naegele's Rule to calculate an expected delivery date, what do you do to the months?

question: Why is caregiver training a crucial part of the discharge process in rehab?

question: Why chat with local community leaders before holding an immunization outreach in their village?

question: Why do safety experts encourage a blame-free reporting culture in hospitals?

question: A patient comes in with diarrhea, stomach cramps, and fatigue. What is an important question to ask during your nursing assessment?

question: Why might a patient's surgical incision fail to heal properly due to poor diet?

question: What is a top public health strategy for preventing neural tube defects?

question: Why do we include a reference list at the end of a report?

question: The principle of sustainability in CBR mainly encourages the use of what?

question: What is the main goal of actively managing the third stage of labor for an anaemic patient?

question: What is the primary reason for encouraging high fluid intake after an intravenous pyelogram?

question: Which of these specimens should NOT be put in the refrigerator if transport is delayed?

question: Quantitative data collection focuses mainly on what type of information?

question: What is the primary reason mothers often give early formula supplementation that nurses should proactively address?

question: A patient finishes metronidazole for amebic dysentery but skips the luminal agent. What is the biggest risk?

question: What type of air pressure is kept inside the operating room to stop outside air from rushing in when doors open?

question: A pregnant patient on insulin therapy tells the nurse she feels shaky, sweaty, and dizzy. What is the immediate nursing action?

options.C: Provide a fast-acting oral carbohydrate source

question: Which dangerous bacterial infection can easily enter through an open Guinea worm wound if someone isn't vaccinated?

question: You are getting ready to repair a perineal tear after delivery. Which drug should you draw up to numb the area?

question: What does the thermic effect of food (TEF) refer to?

question: A patient lies awake for hours before finally falling asleep. What do we call this?

question: Which nursing action helps prevent deep vein thrombosis (DVT) in a paralyzed leg?

question: Which of these is a common symptom of the genitourinary syndrome of menopause?

question: Why are older adults at such a high risk for becoming dehydrated?

question: Which of these is NOT something you should do when managing a sudden laryngospasm?

question: Why is it clinically important to treat pain quickly in emergency care, beyond just making the patient comfortable?

question: Which nutrient takes the most energy for your body to process and digest?

question: How can extreme poverty drive some families to practice early marriage?

question: Why are pelvic floor exercises recommended for women after childbirth?

question: What term describes the socially constructed roles and behaviors that societies consider appropriate for men and women?

question: Which health problem is a well-known long-term risk for patients taking steroids for a long time?

question: Which major nerve provides 'rest-and-digest' signals to speed up activity throughout the GI tract?

explanation: Spot on! The vagus nerve is the primary highway for parasympathetic signals, telling your gut to ramp up digestion and keep things moving. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T011#GNS227_U1_T011_h8)

question: On a lab report, what does a "shift to the left" in white blood cells usually tell the healthcare team?

options.A: An allergic reaction rather than a bacterial infection
options.B: A recovery phase where all blood counts return to normal
options.C: An increased release of immature white blood cells
options.D: A complete failure of the bone marrow to produce cells

explanation: You nailed it! When a severe infection drains the mature white blood cells, the bone marrow starts rushing out baby cells ('bands') early to help out. [learn more](GST114_U2_T4#GST114_U2_T4_h4)

question: Which group of organs gets drugs distributed to them the fastest because of high blood supply?

options.A: Ligaments and tendons
options.B: Bones and resting muscle
options.C: Heart, brain, and liver
options.D: Skin and fatty tissue

explanation: Vial organs get a huge share of the blood pumped by the heart, meaning circulating drugs arrive there almost instantly! [learn more](GNS125_U5_T2#GNS125_U5_T2_h4)

question: What assisted reproductive technique involves injecting a single sperm directly into an egg?

options.A: Intracytoplasmic sperm injection
options.B: Vasectomy reversal
options.C: In vitro fertilization
options.D: Intrauterine insemination

explanation: Intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI) directly places one selected sperm into an egg to overcome severe male factor infertility. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T20#GNS312_U1_T20_h7)

question: Where should a clinical specimen be stored if testing is delayed?

options.A: On an open shelf in the nurses' station
options.B: Inside the staff room food refrigerator
options.C: In a dedicated specimen refrigerator
options.D: Underneath the patient bedside locker

explanation: Specimens requiring delayed processing must go into a specific specimen fridge to avoid contaminating food or clean areas. [learn more](GST114_U2_T14#GST114_U2_T14_h4)

question: What is a common tool managers use to check how happy and satisfied staff are?

options.A: Monthly hospital pharmacy audits
options.B: Anonymous employee satisfaction surveys
options.C: Mandatory physician credentialing files
options.D: Daily patient vital sign flow sheets

explanation: Anonymous surveys let nurses speak their minds freely and honestly about what's working and what's frustrating on the ward. [learn more](GST321_U1_T18#GST321_U1_T18_h6)

question: What event finally tells the secondary oocyte to finish its second division?

options.A: Entry of a sperm cell
options.B: Degeneration of the corpus luteum
options.C: Arrival in the uterus
options.D: A drop in progesterone levels

explanation: Brilliant! The egg waits patiently in the fallopian tube, and the moment a sperm enters, it completes its final cell division. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T9#GNS121_U5_T9_h6)

question: What is the main feature of an ergonomic workplace injury?

options.A: It results only from extreme cold temperatures
options.B: It develops slowly over time from repeated physical strain
options.C: It is caused by breathing in airborne bacteria
options.D: It happens instantly from an explosion or spill

explanation: Ergonomic injuries like carpal tunnel or back strain build up gradually when our bodies are subjected to poor posture and repetitive movements. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T5#GNS225_U7_T5_h5)

question: How are separate sanitary sewer networks different from combined systems?

options.A: They carry human wastewater in dedicated pipes separate from storm runoff
options.B: They only operate during daylight hours when industrial plants are open
options.C: They process all solid waste entirely on-site using chemical agents
options.D: They rely exclusively on open drainage ditches running alongside roads

explanation: Separate systems use one set of pipes for sewage and a completely different set for rainwater. This clever design keeps rain floods from overwhelming the treatment plant with raw waste! [learn more](GST114_U6_T4#GST114_U6_T4_h5)

question: Following a sudden pipeline explosion, a hospital receives dozens of patients with severe burns. What immediate care will these patients need most?

options.A: A high demand for specialized fluid resuscitation, wound care, and pain management
options.B: A sudden requirement for widespread vector control and mosquito net distribution
options.C: An immediate influx of chronic malnutrition cases requiring outpatient nutritional counseling
options.D: A massive need for long-term physical therapy related to chronic stroke rehabilitation

explanation: Burn injuries cause massive fluid loss and intense pain. Nurses must act fast with IV fluids, careful wound dressings, and pain relief! [learn more](GNS315_U1_T7#GNS315_U1_T7_h3)

question: What is the main role of a home care nurse when working with the healthcare team on a slow-healing wound?

options.A: Acting as the eyes and ears to report accurate, up-to-date wound changes to providers
options.B: Ordering all prescription medications without physician approval
options.C: Performing surgical debridement during every home visit
options.D: Diagnosing the underlying systemic disease independently

explanation: You are the vital link! Your accurate updates from the home help doctors, dietitians, and specialists adjust the care plan so the patient heals faster. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T4#GNS324_U3_T4_h6)
